outcome: Composite adverse maternal outcome (urinary or gastrointestinal tract injuries, hemoglobin drop >3 g/dL, blood transfusion, relaparotomy, puerperal fever, prolonged maternal hospitalization, readmission)
cohort: 11,954 women undergoing cesarean delivery at a single tertiary center between 2006 and 2013
finding: Higher surgeon cesarean delivery volume was associated with a lower risk of composite adverse maternal outcomes, primarily driven by reductions in urinary/gastrointestinal injuries, hemoglobin drop >3 g/dL, and prolonged hospitalization.
